newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares continue rising in "genuine" demand.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares continue rising in "genuine" demand.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose with some adding their maximum five percent margin in the Cairo stock market on Thursday, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index added 7.64 points to close at 366.6 in 57.9 million pounds ($17.00 million) worth of trade.
Brokers agreed that prices were still attractive in the market despite the upward trend, which started on Wednesday.
"The market is solid because prices are still attractive to buy," Neveen el-Tahry of Delta-EAB told Reuters. "There is genuine demand. It is alive... Everything is asked for."
"I tell people it is still not too late to buy," said Mohammad Abdullah, Intercapital managing director.
Another move which could affect the market upwards, was the Central Bank's cut of the discount rate on Thursday to 12.25 percent from 12.75 percent.
"The cut may have its impact on the market. But it will not be sudden, nor sharp," Abdullah said.
Many shares rose five percent, the limit imposed by CMA on the rise or fall of stocks.
Commercial International Bank (CIB) had 8.35 million pounds worth of trade. But the share closed 0.08 pounds down to 75.00.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills closed at 85.28 pounds, 4.06 up, when equity worth 4.18 million pounds changed hands.
Suez Cement was the most active share in the cement sector with turnover of 3.8 million pounds. The equity ended 3.12 pounds up to 65.62.

Housing blue chip Heliopolis Housing and Development, added 9.00 pounds to 420 in 2.5 million pounds of trade. Medinet Nasr Housing and Development went 15 pounds up to end at 480 in much smaller volume.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 519.51 from 508.88 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms also rose to 266.42 from 260.82.
Out of the 90 shares traded, 54 ended up, 19 fell and 17 were unchanged.
